issue_context.title: Admission webhook metrics improvement
issue_context.body:
<!-- Feature requests are unlikely to make progress as an issue.

Instead, please suggest enhancements by engaging with SIGs on slack and mailing lists.

A proposal that works through the design along with the implications of the change can be opened as a KEP:
https://git.k8s.io/enhancements/keps#kubernetes-enhancement-proposals-keps
-->

#### What would you like to be added:

- Add a `namespace` label to admission webhook related [metrics](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/metrics/metrics.go#L125-L157)
- Extend the max value of the webhook latency histogram buckets metrics to 10s

#### Why is this needed:
Bad admission webhooks can reject/timeout/fail critical requests like kube-controller-manager (KCM) and kube-scheduler (KS) lease renewal. Such failures are not very visible because the admission webhook metrics do not record the resource or the namespace of a request. Adding a `namespace` label will make such failures easier to detect without increasing the cardinality of the metrics significantly.

The range of the webhook latency histogram 0-2.5s. Some critical requests like leader elections have a 10s default timeout, so the extending the buckets to 10s will allow us to observe the 10s timeout.

/sig instrumentation
/sig api-machinery

review_comments: hm, I'd expect a bucket right at 1s (that's the longest I think a well behaved webhook should be taking). The 5.0 bucket doesn't follow the pattern of the past increases, which are x5 or x4 each time. It might be useful to know the difference between 10s (terrible performance) and 20-29s (absolutely unacceptable). I don't think this is blocking, feel free to make a follow-up.

how is a namespace label not a cardinality problem here? O(10,000) unique namespaces are envisioned in https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/sig-scalability/configs-and-limits/thresholds.md

10k namespaces would be an exceptional case which we can remedy by leveraging https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2305. It's also an existing concern with request metrics which have far greater potential issues for cardinality (which we can also sidestep by explicitly setting bounds for label values).
can you open an issue to track for 1.22? if this represents a regression for ~all clusters, it might need to be reverted before 1.22.0

> can you open an issue to track for 1.22? if this represents a regression for ~all clusters, it might need to be reverted before 1.22.0

opened https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/104008

I'd be surprised if it affected normal clusters. But reflecting on it, it actually does make sense that this would happen on a test cluster, since we tend to generate namespaces on a per-test basis (i.e. a ton of namespace churn). Even so, probably not a bad idea to revert.
namespace churn can happen in normal clusters too... anything that uses namespaces for bounded operations (builds,  jobs, etc) is likely to frequently create/delete namespaces
I also don't think it's a good idea for controllers to add namespace labels to metrics (e.g. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102523)

we found the `apiserver_admission_controller_admission_duration_seconds_bucket` metric caused 1165536 time series on a cluster with 112 namespaces. without digging deeper this caused prometheus to consume ~7gb of ram within seconds rendering default nodes notready very fast.
It's nice to have namespace visibility, though.. maybe we should have a mode where you can turn on a namespace metric explicitly via flags.
I believe it's the churn, not the existing number of namespaces that's causing this @s-urbaniak
agreed, yes, but the added cardinality amplifies.

> It's nice to have namespace visibility, though..

I can agree with that point for counters and gauges, but I don't think this is safe or really needed for histograms since we will most likely never use this information to create SLOs or any latency-based alert.
In addition to that, the valuable information for the user here is to know which namespaces the rejection is coming from. This is a piece of information that could be present in the logs and we could narrow the metric responsibility to only report rejections and 5XX error codes that could then be used in actual alerts.
